task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (design): pick and design among ISS-0442's options (a) Jason.OrderedObject round trip, (b) targeted top-level-status-only substitution with the demonstrated PASS/PASS nested-collision risk designed around structurally, (c) correct the reviewability claim everywhere instead -- for making `--autofix`'s rewrite of a handoff JSON's top-level `status` field produce a minimal diff instead of ISSUE-FIXER's reproduced 88-line whole-file rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: A real recommendation with reasoning about tradeoffs is made, not just a restatement of the three options
jason dependency version/capability for option (a) checked against what mix.exs/mix.lock actually pin

If (b) is chosen, the substitution is position-precise (structurally distinguishes the top-level status key from any nested status field, e.g. result.status) and the algorithm is specified precisely enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgment calls
If (c) is chosen, every location making the false reviewability claim is enumerated
Design explicitly preserves the FAIL/missing/null/non-string refusal behaviour verified in ISS-0440
Design explicitly preserves the no-flag CI path (unaffected)
No implementation code in the design document -- signatures/specs/algorithm description only

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/iss0442-lint-handoffs-minimal-diff-autofix.md. Checked mix.exs/mix.lock directly: jason is pinned to 1.4.5 via `~> 1.4`, and Jason.OrderedObject is not present in 1.4.5 (shipped later in the 1.x line) -- confirming ISSUE-FIXER's finding. Went further than the prior diagnosis on option (a): even with OrderedObject available, `pretty: true` re-encoding still reflows formatting (effect (2) from the diagnosis, e.g. inline arrays exploding to one-per-line) independently of key order (effect (1)) -- so (a) would only fix effect (1) and still fail the actual minimal-diff goal, on top of forcing a decode-shape fork across autofix_file/1 and the H1-H4 checks. Recommended and designed option (b): a structural, depth- and position-aware raw-text scan (tracks JSON nesting depth via brace/bracket counting outside of strings, and distinguishes a depth-1 KEY string from any string by checking whether the next non-whitespace char after its closing quote is ':') that can only ever match the top-level `status` member and structurally cannot match a nested `result.status`, regardless of file ordering -- directly closing ISSUE-FIXER's demonstrated PASS/PASS collision by construction rather than by incidental serialization order. Because it never decodes+re-encodes the document, it is immune to both effect (1) and effect (2): the resulting diff is exactly the one status value token, and the file's original trailing-newline convention is preserved automatically (no more forced `<> "\n"` append). Specified two new function shapes (rewrite_top_level_status!/3, splice_top_level_status/2) replacing write_json!/2 (confirmed via grep its only call site is the one being replaced), and a step-by-step scan/splice algorithm including last-key-wins handling for a malformed duplicate-key document (mirroring Jason.decode/1's own semantics) and an explicit fail-loud (never fall back to whole-file re-encode) path for the invariant-violation case where the raw-text scan disagrees with what Jason.decode/1 already found. Section 1.2 evaluated (c) and enumerated every place the reviewability claim could be made (ISS-0442.yaml itself, the --autofix @moduledoc, write_json!/2's own comment, SECURITY-REVIEWER's ISS-0440 sign-off) and rejected (c) as premature since (b) is proportionate. Section 3 explicitly states preservation of the FAIL/missing/non-string refusal branches (autofix_file/1's case expression unchanged in every branch but one) and of the no-flag CI path (run/1's `if autofix?` guard means none of the changed functions are ever invoked without --autofix). Section 4 lists open questions (exact exception type for the invariant-violation raise; suggested regression fixtures for TEST-DESIGNER) without resolving them, per CODE-DESIGNER's mandate not to silently pick an unstated assumption. No implementation code included -- reviewed the full file for literal Elixir code blocks/closures (the specific class of violation CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard-failed on this branch's earlier REQ-157 rework) and found none; all code-styled inline spans are function-name/arity references (e.g. rewrite_top_level_status!/3) or @spec-shaped type signatures, consistent with this project's design-doc convention.
result.next_action: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR: verify every ISS-0442 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element, confirm no implementation code is present, and confirm the algorithm is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to build from without further judgment calls.
